claims.statement: The European Commission describes local flexibility markets as central to unlocking demand-side flexibility and is developing common demand-response rules while national markets develop at different rates.
The EU Data Act has applied since September 2025 and gives business users access to and the ability to share raw data generated by connected products including industrial machinery.

contrary_evidence: Local flexibility markets remain uneven across Europe, so a standard product may arrive before sufficient transaction volume in Poland.
Large aggregators and market platforms already maintain internal settlement systems and may expose only final statements.

economics.acquisition_route: Technical integrations and revenue-leakage audits for a few small aggregators, then channel sales via device installers and energy consultants
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A plausible 5-7 year path would require about 100,000-150,000 active assets across several markets, 5-7 PLN monthly average revenue per asset, strong software margins, and substantial retained founder equity
economics.founder_time: Approximately 12-16 hours per week during initial integrations, with market-law review outsourced
economics.gross_margin_basis: Cloud data processing and support less meter-connectivity, security, and implementation costs
economics.payback: The operator should recover fees through reduced manual settlement, corrected allocations, and fewer owner disputes; the size of leakage must be established from sample portfolios
economics.pricing: Approximately 4-8 PLN per active asset per month plus 0.25-0.75% of reconciled flexibility revenue
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every dispatch and monthly owner statement recurs; historical baselines increase switching cost

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Cross-asset response and exception data could improve baseline selection, detect missing revenue, and establish trusted performance histories for portfolios
fingerprint.customer: EU demand-response aggregators, energy-service companies, and installers managing distributed flexible assets
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Partner with battery and heat-pump installers, energy consultants, and smaller aggregators that lack internal settlement engineering
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Data ingestion, baseline versioning, shadow invoices, exception queues, and asset-owner statements; sell as SaaS without initially becoming an aggregator or settlement bank
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The portfolio operator pays per active asset and a small percentage when an event is reconciled and an owner statement is issued
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A dispatch or local-flexibility event completes but delivered volume, baseline adjustments, penalties, and downstream owner shares must be reconstructed from several systems

founder_fit: Time-series modelling, anomaly detection, and reconciliation fit the founder's data-science background
Family access to renewable installations can support device-data prototyping
The product is technical and asynchronous rather than relationship-heavy once integrations are live
risks: Incorrect baselines could misallocate money and undermine trust
Energy-market roles and data permissions differ by country
Aggregators may treat settlement logic as strategic and refuse external dependence
Integration and cybersecurity requirements may be costly

structure.commercial_archetype: Meter-point SaaS plus a small fee on reconciled flexibility revenue
structure.control_point: The versioned baseline and event receipt mapping operator dispatch, meter interval, market result, and asset-owner allocation
structure.critical_dependency: Timely access to granular meter and dispatch data plus commercial contracts that recognise the reconciliation method

thesis: Aggregators operating portfolios of household batteries, heat pumps, EV chargers, and commercial loads could use an independent shadow-settlement ledger that reconstructs dispatch delivery, baseline, penalties, and asset-owner revenue allocation before money moves. The initial product would reconcile and issue signed statements rather than itself participate in electricity markets or hold customer funds.
title: FlexSettle Shadow Ledger
uncertainties: How much unreconciled value smaller aggregators currently lose
Which Polish or nearby market exposes sufficient event-level data
Whether owner contracts permit an independent shadow ledger to resolve disputes
Whether device data are sufficiently complete and comparable across manufacturers
